rows.title: Reset-semantic substrate corruption as a convergent failure regime in repeated bounded self-improvement
rows.exact_prediction: In a repeated bounded self-improvement loop on executable Gym-style or repository-training substrates, edits that change reset/initialization semantics while preserving or improving the fixed evaluator's short-run score will produce lower downstream training performance than matched edits that change only step dynamics; moreover, the probability or severity of below-no-training performance will increase across rounds when corrupted artifacts are carried forward, even after controlling for task distribution, diversity, step-transition validity, code complexity, and training budget.
rows.strongest_same_information_baseline: A compound distribution-shift/negative-transfer plus coupled-optimization baseline that receives the same generated-task distribution, step-transition statistics, reward signal, memory/designer state, learner state, training budget, and evaluator feedback, and attributes below-baseline outcomes to non-reset mismatch or instability.
rows.falsifier_expression: Using released or easily constructed Gym-style executable environments, create a small preregistered repeated-round study with matched edit pairs: one edit changes reset/initialization only, the other changes step dynamics only, while holding task goal, reward scale, transition difficulty/diversity, code complexity, training budget, and evaluator score fixed. Train identical learners after each edit and across carried rounds. The candidate is falsified if reset-only edits do not produce more below-no-training outcomes or more recurrence than step-only edits after these controls. A secondary AI4AI-Bench-side check can statically/dynamically diff submitted rewrites for initialization, seeding, checkpoint loading, dataloader construction, environment construction, and reset-call changes and test whether those changes predict below-0.1 cells after controlling for other code-change features.
rows.endpoint_headroom_requirement: The effect must exceed ordinary distribution-shift and coupled-optimization controls under matched information; a merely nonzero rate of below-baseline edits is insufficient because 124/290 already establishes aggregate regression, not reset-specific causation.

rows.title: Complex-description boundary in end-to-end 3D world construction
rows.exact_prediction: After matching prompt length, number of constraints, referential ambiguity, asset count, rubric difficulty, and spatial-quantity demand, Complex Description/Scene Restatement queries will still show lower Pass@1 and a higher concentration of cross-stage intent-to-layout/render binding failures than other VWE-Bench query types; clarifying text alone will not close the gap unless it also resolves executable binding.
rows.strongest_same_information_baseline: A matched long-context plus spatial-grounding baseline that uses query length, constraint count, ambiguity, asset count, distance/angle/object-count demands, and stage-specific grounding/editing errors to predict Pass@1.
rows.falsifier_expression: Using released VWE-Bench/VibeWorlding-Gym units, construct a matched comparison: sample Complex Description/Scene Restatement failures and easier-query controls matched on length, constraint count, asset count, rubric difficulty, and spatial-quantity demand; annotate stage-specific errors; optionally generate clarified-query versions. The falsifier is passed if query type no longer predicts Pass@1 or stage-specific binding failure after these controls.
rows.endpoint_headroom_requirement: To remain paperable beyond a benchmark observation, the candidate needs a prospective pre-outcome feature or controlled intervention that predicts the below-50% basin and separates executable cross-stage binding from long-context, generic underspecification, and spatial-grounding baselines.

rows.title: Stateful-feedback validity horizon for self-evolving skill controllers
rows.exact_prediction: Under matched model, task distribution, initial feedback, update budget, and harness-state statistics, an update schedule selected from initial single-turn feedback will fail or stagnate when later multi-turn interactions reveal defects outside the initial feedback basis; a stateful feedback-refresh controller will improve on those same units. A generic stale-supervision/nonstationarity baseline given the same feedback recency and occupancy statistics will not predict the basis-mismatch split.
rows.strongest_same_information_baseline: A stale-supervision/nonstationary online-learning baseline that receives the same early and later feedback samples, recency, sample size, occupancy/domain-shift statistics, and update budget, and predicts performance solely from distribution shift and fresh-information availability.
rows.falsifier_expression: Using the released or reproducible SkillEvo substrate, create matched units with the same initial single-turn feedback and early TSR trajectory. In one arm, keep later defects within the initially revealed gap classes; in the other, introduce later multi-turn defects outside that class while matching task difficulty, model, revision budget, governance, and feedback quantity. Compare an initial-feedback-selected schedule against a stateful feedback-refresh schedule and a generic stale-supervision/nonstationarity baseline. If the generic baseline predicts the split equally well, reject the new problem formulation.
rows.endpoint_headroom_requirement: The residual must appear on prospective later-round defects before observing endpoint TSR, not by post hoc selection of trajectories where multi-turn feedback wins. It must survive matched feedback quantity, recency, task difficulty, governance action, and harness-state statistics.
